preamble: The Middle Korean vowel ㆍ (arae-a), reconstructed as [ʌ], was lost from almost all modern Korean varieties; while it usually became [a] in first syllables and [ɨ] elsewhere, a number of words rounded it to [o]. Standard Korean shows this in 소매 'sleeve' from Middle Korean ᄉᆞᄆᆡ /sʌ.mʌj/, and Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Chungcheong and Hamgyong dialects round it after the labial ㅍ, as in 포리 'fly' beside standard 파리, from Middle Korean ᄑᆞ리.

examples.note: The first-syllable arae-a became [o] in the standard language, where most such words have [a].
Wiktionary attributes the [o] to rounding after the labial ㅍ; the form is recorded for Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Chungcheong, Hamgyong and Yukjin dialects.

period: Late Middle Korean to Modern Korean
